criteria.reasoning: The plan's ask is "**$95,000**" ("Propose **$95,000 over two years**"). The criterion requires a single figure of $80,000 and names $95,000 as a failing amount.

The plan caps the ask at "4 × $25,000 = $100,000". It identifies "the **$25,000 Spring Gala presenting sponsorship of 2023**" as the household's largest gift and calls the $20,000 Family Fund gift only "the next largest". That is the corporate sponsorship the criterion names as a failing choice.

The plan proposes "$95,000 over two years for the Adult Literacy Program", covering the Upriver site and Tutor Corps, with alternatives only within the program. It states "No Open Doors or Eastside Branch option will be raised".
The plan states "**No naming opportunity** of any kind will be offered (policy A5)." No naming option appears anywhere else in the brief.

Recognition is "**Anonymous.**" The gift "will not appear in the annual report, on any donor wall or in any announcement; it will be acknowledged privately by letter". The brief also directs that the CRM recognition name be changed to Anonymous.

The brief says "**Ask Celeste.**", quoting Martin: "Celeste runs our giving". It states Martin is welcome at the meeting "but the ask is made to Celeste", and his 2022 building interest "is not the plan."

The meeting is arranged through the business email: "Teresa emails Celeste this week at **celeste@vandermolenmarine.com**, the CRM's alternate email". The criterion fails any use of the vandermolenmarine.com addresses.
The team is "**Teresa Lindahl with Lillian Cho**". The brief notes Celeste asked for Lillian and that Lillian "has made her FY27 gift and has no conflict". No one else is on the team.
The brief states "**Gregory Hale has no role.**", citing his arbitration disclosure and section 4 of the COI Policy. It adds "Teresa will thank him for his 2026-09-21 offer and decline it."

Talking point 5 discloses the anonymous gift by name and amount: "Peer example: Ingrid Rasmussen ... and her family have just made a $100,000 gift to the Adult Literacy Endowment. Lillian can mention it".
The plan sets the "**Ask meeting: the week of October 5, 2026** ... before the advisor meeting". That is before the mid-October advisor meeting, which the criterion fails.

The facts the brief states about the couple all appear in the files: their gifts, Celeste's tutoring since 2023, the quotations from 2026-06-10, the home address, the Family Fund, the $382,000 capacity and inclination 4. The policy breaches (the Rasmussen disclosure, the business email, the cap) are misapplied rules judged elsewhere, and none is an invented fact about the donors.
